title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding
source: We introduce a new language representation model called BERT, which stands for Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers. Unlike recent language representation models, BERT is designed to pre-train deep bidirectional representations from unlabeled text by jointly conditioning on both left and right context in all layers. As a result, the pre-trained BERT model can be fine-tuned with just one additional output layer to create state-of-the-art models for a wide range of tasks, such as question answering and language inference, without substantial task-specific architecture modifications. BERT is conceptually simple and empirically powerful. It obtains new state-of-the-art results on eleven natural language processing tasks, including pushing the GLUE score to 80.5%, MultiNLI accuracy to 86.7%, and SQuAD v1.1 question answering Test F1 to 93.2.
target_summary: BERT introduces deep bidirectional Transformer pre-training that achieves state-of-the-art across 11 NLP benchmarks with simple task-specific fine-tuning.

title: Attention Is All You Need
source: The dominant sequence transduction models are based on complex recurrent or convolutional neural networks that include an encoder and a decoder. The best performing models also connect the encoder and decoder through an attention mechanism. We propose a new simple network architecture, the Transformer, based solely on attention mechanisms, dispensing with recurrence and convolutions entirely. Experiments on two machine translation tasks show these models to be superior in quality while being more parallelizable and requiring significantly less time to train. Our model achieves 28.4 BLEU on the WMT 2014 English-to-German translation task, improving over the existing best results, including ensembles, by over 2 BLEU.
target_summary: The Transformer replaces recurrence and convolutions entirely with multi-head self-attention, achieving superior translation quality and faster parallel training.

title: Longformer: The Long-Document Transformer
source: Transformer-based models are unable to process long sequences due to their self-attention operation, which scales quadratically with the sequence length. To address this limitation, we present Longformer with an attention mechanism that scales linearly with sequence length, making it easy to process documents of thousands of tokens or longer. Longformer's attention mechanism is a plug-and-play replacement for the standard self-attention and combines a local windowed attention with a task-motivated global attention. Following prior work on long-sequence Transformers, we evaluate Longformer on character-level language modeling and achieve state-of-the-art results on text8 and enwik8.
target_summary: Longformer introduces a linear-scaling attention mechanism combining local windowed and global attention to process thousands of tokens efficiently.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP Tasks
source: Large pre-trained language models have been shown to store factual knowledge in their parameters, and achieve state-of-the-art results when fine-tuned on downstream NLP tasks. However, their ability to access and precisely manipulate knowledge is still limited, and whereupon on knowledge-intensive tasks, their performance falls behind task-specific architectures. In this work, we develop a general-purpose fine-tuning recipe for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) — models which combine pre-trained parametric and non-parametric memory for language generation. We introduce RAG models where the parametric memory is a pre-trained seq2seq model and the non-parametric memory is a dense vector index of Wikipedia, accessed with a pre-trained neural retriever.
target_summary: RAG pairs parametric seq2seq transformers with non-parametric dense neural retrieval to improve factual knowledge retrieval and text generation.

title: Dense Passage Retrieval for Open-Domain Question Answering
source: Open-domain question answering relies on efficient passage retrieval to select candidate contexts for reading comprehension. Traditionally, retrieval has been dominated by sparse vector space models such as TF-IDF or BM25. In this work, we show that retrieval can be practically implemented using dense representations, where embeddings are learned from a small number of questions and passages by a simple dual-encoder framework. When evaluated on a wide range of open-domain QA datasets, our dense retriever out-performs a strong BM25 system by 9%-19% absolute top-20 retrieval accuracy, establishing a new state of the art.
target_summary: Dense Passage Retrieval uses a dual-encoder architecture that dramatically outperforms BM25 lexical retrieval on open-domain question answering.
